newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SAFRICA UNDER FIRE AFTER HEAVY TEST DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SAFRICA UNDER FIRE AFTER HEAVY TEST DEFEAT.

text.p: South Africa's cricketers were derided as no-hopers on Wednesday after their crushing defeat by Australia in the first test, one of the worst they have ever suffered.
Local sports commentators who were saying six days ago that the three-test series would give the world its unofficial test champions were describing the series as a no-contest.
"To judge by the first test, Australia are better than their opponents (South Africa) at this type of cricket," Die Burger newspaper said in an editorial on the defeat.
"South Africa's prospects in the following two tests look dire, because they have no better players to fall back on," it said.

Australia wrapped up the opening test on the final day on Tuesday with more than two sessions left, winning by an innings and 196 runs. It was South Africa's first defeat by an innings since 1964-65 when they lost by an innings and 104 runs to England in Durban.
Die Burger quoted Kepler Wessels, predecessor to Hansie Cronje as captain of the team, as saying questions had to be asked about leadership.
"Somebody must take the lead on the pitch," Wessels said. Asked by the paper if Cronje's leadership was adequate, he replied: "Did it look like it?"

Wessels said the team needed "big-hearted" players such as Brian McMillan who could withstand the pressures of test cricket. All-rounder McMillan was not considered for the first test because of injury.
Roy McLean, a South African batting hero from the 1960s, said of the home team's batting performance at the Wanderers:
"I haven't seen such a pathetic batting display for a long time... There comes a time when old players must make way for new ones."
South African cricket writers described their team variously as "matchstick men" and paddlers in a leaky canoe.

"The truth of the matter is that South Africa, on the form of the first test, does not rank among the superpowers of the game such as Australia, Pakistan and the West Indies," Independent Newspapers group correspondent Michael Owen-Smith wrote.
"The current series is probably beyond South Africa's winning."

The Cape Times newspaper carried a cartoon in which a housewife remarks: "This new cookbook says the perfect time to boil an egg is exactly the time it takes for four South African batsmen to go out."
The second test starts in Port Elizabeth on March 14.
